tender.description: To correct the extension of the established Dynamic Purchasing System (“DPS”) for the procurement of passenger transport services, excluding local bus services until March 2028

lots.description:
The Vale of Glamorgan Council is publishing this Notice in relation to the existing Dynamic Purchasing System (DPS) for Passenger Transport Services (excluding Local Bus Services).
The Contract Notice published on 5 August 2025 under reference 2025/S 000-046223 incorrectly stated the end date of the DPS as 31 July 2026.
The Council has identified that this was an administrative error in the published notice. The intended end date of the DPS was 31 March 2028.
This notice therefore corrects the previously published information so that the published record accurately reflects the intended period of validity of the DPS. To correct an error contained within the Extension notice
Organisations are invited to submit a Pre-Qualification Questionnaire to gain access to the Council’s Dynamic Purchasing System (“DPS”)
for Passenger Transport Services.
Successful applicants to the DPS will then, via mini competitions, be requested to submit offers for a variety of Passenger Transport
Services, including Mainstream and Additional Learning Needs (“ALN”) School Transport services.

tender.reviewDetails:
The Vale of Glamorgan Council will incorporate a minimum 10 calendar day standstill period at the point information on the award of the contract is communicated to tenderers.  This period allows unsuccessful tenderers to seek further debriefing from the Council before the contract is entered into.  Applicants have 2 working days from the notification of the award decision to request additional debriefing and that information has to be provided a minimum of 3 working days before the expiry of the standstill period.  Such additional information should be requested from the Council.
If an appeal regarding the award of a contract has not been successfully resolved the Public Contracts Regulations 20014  (SI 2006 No 102) provide for aggrieved parties who have been harmed or are at risk of harm by a breach of the rules to take action in the High Court (England, Wales and Northern Ireland).  Any such action must be brought promptly (generally within 3 months).  Where a contract has not been entered into the Court may order the setting aside of the award decision or order the authority to amend any document and may award damages.  If the contract has been entered into the Court may only award damages.

tender.title: ASEAN-UK SAGE
tender.description:
The ASEAN-UK SAGE programme is a six-year Business Case  funded by the UK’s Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) through the UK Mission to ASEAN. Delivered in two phases, the UK Mission to ASEAN is now seeking eligible organisation(s) to deliver a three-year Phase 2. 
Phase 2 will run for three UK financial years, from August 2026 to March 2029, with a total budget of £9,000,000. It will be delivered by a lead organisation under an agreement with the UK Mission to ASEAN, supported by downstream partners as needed. 
The focus of ASEAN-UK SAGE is to support inclusive and equitable quality education for children across Southeast Asia Region in close collaboration with ASEAN secretariat, especially for girls and the most marginalised, contributing to regional integration and narrowing of development disparities between ASEAN Member States (AMS) .  
The emphasis in Phase 2 will be on the use of evidence to improve learning outcomes and inclusion, especially for priority countries in the region.

tender.title: Construction, Maintenance and Minor Works Framework
tender.description:
Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council gives notice of its intention to award a Construction and Minor Works Framework for the delivery of construction, maintenance, repair, refurbishment and associated minor works required by Council during the framework term, which is three years.
The proposed framework is intended to provide the Council with access to suitably experienced and competent contractors capable of delivering a range of planned, reactive and project-based works across the Council estate. The scope will include, but is not limited to, general building works, minor civil works, repair and maintenance activities, small-scale refurbishment, enabling works and associated construction-related services.
The proposed framework will offer access to a range of construction and minor works trades and disciplines, including painting and decorating, plastering, plumbing, Gas Safe engineering, joinery, drywall and ceilings, skilled labour, general labouring, fence erection, glazing, bricklaying and stonemasonry, tiling, welding and roofing, playpark installations.
The estimated total value of the Framework over its term is £1,500,000. This estimate is provided for transparency and planning purposes only and does not constitute a guarantee of volume of work or number of call-off contracts to be awarded under the Framework.
The framework will be used exclusively for works and contractors/individuals located within the borough area of Causeway Coast and Glens Borough Council.
It is intended to support the efficient, compliant and timely delivery of Council requirements across the Borough whilst providing support to local firms through direct procurement and ensuring that works are procured and delivered in a manner that meets Council’s operational needs, statutory responsibilities and commitment to transparency in public procurement.
The framework is not intended to confer exclusivity on any single supplier, and any subsequent call-off arrangements will be managed in accordance with the terms of the Framework and the applicable requirements of the Procurement Act 2023 and the Procurement Regulations 2024.
Council considers that the framework is particularly suitable for small and medium-sized enterprises. The nature, scale and geographic focus of the works are expected to provide opportunities for local and regional contractors, including SMEs, to participate as subcontractors.
Council will seek to ensure that the procurement documentation is proportionate, accessible and clear, with requirements set at a level that encourage participation from SMEs and to reduce unnecessary barriers to competition.
In publishing this notice, the Council is providing advance transparency to the market regarding its intention to establish and award the framework. This notice is intended to inform interested suppliers of the Council’s proposed approach and to support openness, accountability and understanding of the Council’s procurement decisions.
Publication of this notice does not create any binding commitment to award the framework, nor does it prevent the Council from amending, delaying or discontinuing the proposed procurement where it considers it appropriate to do so.

tender.title: Tender for Clerk of Works service for Warm Home local Grant
tender.description: This new service will act as an independent, technical auditor to verify the design and installation of energy efficiency and low carbon heating measures within Warm Homes Local Grant. It is expected this service will focus on certain measures, particularly External/Internal Wall Insulation, and Air Source Heat Pumps, following the recent National Audit Office report into failures with insulation. The expectation is that by implementing a Clerk of Works service we can assure the quality of designs and installations undertaken by the programme to support residents.

lots.description: GLA intends for all External Wall Insulation, Internal Wall Insulation and Air Source Heat Pump installations to be reviewed by the Clerk of Works, plus a selection of other properties, with the aim to review 15% of properties delivered under the WHLG programme. Under the WHSHF programme, the intention is to undertake a desktop review of 9% of properties and on-site reviews of 1% of the properties completed. This  aligns with the requirements within the Grant Funding Agreement for independent quality assurance under the WHSHF programme.
